trials.notes: Correctly chose WP_HTML_Tag_Processor for a flat, byte-preserving class edit. All calls are documented: next_tag, set_bookmark, seek, add_class, and get_updated_html. Uses the intended one-pass scan, repeatedly moves one literal bookmark to the latest H2, seeks back, and returns updated HTML. No _doing_it_wrong records.

Same correct Tag Processor scan-and-bookmark pattern as the reference, with documented release_bookmark cleanup. All API usage appears in the rendered docs, and the no-H2 fallback returns the original input. No _doing_it_wrong records.

Correct processor and documented APIs throughout: next_tag, is_tag_closer, set_bookmark, seek, add_class, release_bookmark, and get_updated_html. The is_tag_closer guard is redundant because next_tag('h2') skips closers by default, but it is harmless. Otherwise follows the intended bookmark pattern and handles no-match cleanly.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed across the trials: each execution.json reports 6/6 passing cases and no _doing_it_wrong records. The docs did well on the core ideas: 'Which processor should I use?' points flat, position-based class edits to WP_HTML_Tag_Processor; 'Finding tags' and next_tag() document string queries, ASCII case-insensitive tag matching, and that comments/raw text are not matched as tags; 'Bookmarks' explicitly explains re-setting one bookmark name to remember the last matching tag; add_class() explains creation/appending with existing classes; get_updated_html() explains byte-preserving output. The only near-miss is trial-3's redundant closer check, suggesting the default closer policy is easy to miss. Incomplete input was not part of these cases; the docs mention paused_at_incomplete_token(), but the candidates did not need an explicit completeness policy for this task.

doc_gaps.problem: The default 'tag_closers' => 'skip' behavior is present but easy to miss; trial-3 defensively checked is_tag_closer() after a simple string query.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short example stating that next_tag('h2') visits opening H2 tags only, and that callers should pass array('tag_name' => 'h2', 'tag_closers' => 'visit') only when closing tags are needed.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs explain that false can mean incomplete trailing syntax, but do not clearly connect that to mutation policy after earlier successful matches.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add guidance that callers requiring complete input should check paused_at_incomplete_token() after draining the scan, while callers editing already-matched complete tokens may still use get_updated_html(), which preserves untouched incomplete trailing bytes.

doc_gaps.location: html-tag-processor.md: Method Index and private method sections
doc_gaps.problem: Rendered docs expose private methods beside public methods, increasing the risk that doc-only readers treat private helpers as callable API.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Group public APIs separately from private/internal implementation methods, or mark private method sections with a clear 'not part of the public API' warning.
